text:
Anna L.: quick heads-up — customer 'MapleBank' wants a supported flow to grant their legal ops time-limited access to archived audit evidence (KMS-wrapped blobs) for an external regulator audit. They want: 1) a 4-hour access SLA, 2) cryptographic proof of key unwrap attestation, and 3) exportable chain-of-custody. any thoughts?

Sam C.: big ask but doable. options: a) customer-managed temporary escrow key we sign/approve, b) Redwood concierge unseal under ticketed workflow, or c) out-of-band HSM attestation delivered as part of export. each has tradeoffs for risk & compliance.

Maria N.: retention/expunge concerns — if we enable unseal, we need a strict policy that the unsealed copy is ephemeral and automatically garbage-collected. we should surface retention tier in UI/API.

Jordan K.: prototype CLI for the concierge path (manual approval) could look like:
```
redwood evidence unseal --tenant maplebank --evidence-id 12345 --duration 4h --approver @legal_ops
```
that would: create an audit ticket, produce an HSM sig for the unwrap op, and stream the export to the approved destination.

SecurityBot: checklist: 1) MFA approval from 2 people, 2) signed HSM attestation + timestamp, 3) immutable audit log entry (WORM), 4) retention TTL on exported object, 5) legal confirmation of export destination.

Legal Ops: manual unseal by Redwood concierge is okay if we get a full approval trail + export manifest and proof-of-handshake with the customer's KMS. can't accept undocumented manual processes. also need contract addendum for temporary key custody.

Sam C.: For SLA sizing: concierge unseals are labor-heavy. to hit 4h we need an on-call rota + a runbook with checklist automation. alternative — let customer hold an escrow key in their KMS with a signed policy that allows Redwood to call Unwrap under conditions; then it's programmable and scales.

Ops Oncall: what's the expected QPS for these? if it's per-audit (1/day–1/week), concierge might be fine. if several customers ask concurrently it balloons. need capacity guardrails.

Anna L.: proposed next steps: 1) spike a 'temporary-escrow' design doc (owner: Jordan), 2) draft contract language for temporary custody (owner: Legal Ops), 3) build minimal concierge runbook + CLI prototype (owner: Sam), 4) security checklist turned into gating tests (owner: Maria). target: RFC and sample SLA by EOW.

Jordan K.: I'll start the doc and include sequence diagrams (handshake, attestation, export manifest). will call out UX decisions: console flow vs API-only for first-release.

Maria N.: i'll convert the checklist into automated tests for the runbook (audit log integrity / TTL enforcement).

Legal Ops: I'll draft the addendum and list the customer contract fields we need (scope, duration, audit witness, indemnity).

Anna L.: cool. pinging @SecurityBot and @Ops Oncall for visibility. if anyone has previous audit export wording that worked, drop links here. :+1:

Sam C.: also to consider — can we reduce scope by offering an 'observer' export (redact PII) as a lower-risk option for some regulators.

Anna L.: noted. we'll capture that as a product option in the doc. thanks all.
